speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located and how long you've had the fever and skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any red rings or bull's-eye rash on your skin, and have you observed any ticks on your body or clothing recently? I need to know if you've had any headaches, stiff neck, or facial drooping as well.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists following a camping trip in Minnesota is highly suggestive of secondary syphilis, rather than Lyme disease. To confirm this, I need to rule out other causes of monoarthritis and verify the serological status. REQUEST TEST: RPR, Syphilis IgG/IgM, CBC, ESR, CRP, Joint Aspirate Gram Stain and Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RPR: Not performed; Syphilis IgG/IgM: Not performed; CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR: Not performed; CRP: Not performed; Joint Aspirate Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen; Joint Aspirate Culture: Pending

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate confirms gonococcal arthritis. Given the recent camping history, I must rule out concurrent Lyme disease, so I will request specific Lyme serology. REQUEST TEST: Lyme IgM/IgG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lyme IgM: Negative; Lyme IgG: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Lyme serology and the presence of Gram-negative diplococci in the joint aspirate confirm Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
